index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure presents a hierarchical taxonomy of visual-spatial intelligence capabilities, structured as a flowchart with three main columns representing input, processing, and output components. The global layout is left-to-right, with four rectangular boxes aligned vertically on the far left serving as foundational cognitive inputs. These are labeled 'Visual Perception', 'Spatial Reasoning', 'Temporal Processing', and 'Linguistic Intelligence'. All four inputs converge via straight black lines into two central rounded rectangular modules: 'Egocentric-allocentric Transformation' positioned above 'Relational Reasoning'. These central modules represent core processing stages in the visual-spatial intelligence framework. From each of these central modules, branches extend to the right into three output components, also represented as rounded rectangles. The 'Egocentric-allocentric Transformation' module connects to 'Visuospatial Working Memory' and 'Perspective Visualization'. The 'Relational Reasoning' module connects to 'Distance', 'Direction', and 'Visuospatial Common Sense'. All connections are depicted using solid black lines without arrows, indicating a directional flow from left to right but without explicit arrowheads. The entire diagram uses black text on white background with uniform black borders around all shapes; there are no colors or shading. The visual style is minimalist and schematic, emphasizing clarity of relationships over aesthetic embellishment. The figure caption explicitly identifies this as a taxonomy of visual-spatial intelligence capabilities, suggesting it categorizes and organizes cognitive functions involved in spatial cognition. The structure implies that foundational cognitive abilities feed into higher-order transformations and reasoning processes, which then yield specific spatial competencies such as memory, visualization, distance/direction estimation, and common sense reasoning about space.
